Allusion

uh-LOO-zhun · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Allusion is an indirect or passing reference to something, often a work of literature, art, or history, without mentioning it directly.

When the coach called the losing streak 'our own little Trojan War,' the whole team understood the allusion to a long, drawn-out struggle.

Worked Example

The novelist's title, 'A Brave New World Indeed,' is an allusion to Aldous Huxley's famous book, inviting readers to think about the two stories side by side.

An allusion doesn't explain itself -- it trusts the listener or reader to recognize the reference on their own.

How Allusion Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

reference

reference: a mention of something, especially indirectly

insinuation

insinuation: an indirect or crafty suggestion

Antonyms

explicitness

explicitness: the quality of being stated in clear, direct detail

bluntness

bluntness: very direct and plain speech, without subtlety

How Strong Is It? — hint → allusion → quotation

hint vs. allusion

hint vs. allusion: A hint is the mildest, vaguest suggestion of something.

quotation vs. allusion

quotation vs. allusion: A quotation is an exact, direct repetition of someone else's words -- far more direct than an allusion.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of allusion.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — al-

prefix — al-: variant of ad-, 'toward' (Latin)

root — lus

root — lus: to play (from Latin ludere, past participle lusum -- not a standalone English word, but the same disguised root in illusion, delusion, and elude)

suffix — -ion

suffix — -ion: act or result of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Allusion comes from Latin ad- ('toward') + ludere ('to play') -- al- + lus + -ion, literally 'a playing toward' something. The same lud-/lus- root, in disguise, shows up in illusion, delusion, and elude -- all words about things not being quite what they directly seem.

Use the root in a new word: elude

Use the root in a new word: elude: The clever fox managed to elude the hunting dogs for nearly an hour.

Word Choice

Allusion is a favorite word in literature and writing classes -- watch its spelling closely, since it's easily confused with the unrelated word 'illusion' (a false belief or deceptive appearance).
